messages:
maria_support: Hey team — ACME reported failures on /v1/embeddings after a client-side switch to NDJSON streaming. They see 400 'embedding vector size mismatch'. Happened after they updated their batching.

jonathan_sre: Can you paste the raw request they sent (redact tokens) and the Content-Type header?

maria_support: Customer pasted this curl (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/x-ndjson\" \n  --data-binary $'{"input":"hello world"}\n{"input":"[0.003,0.12,0.21, ...]"}\n'
```
They said they send many lines; some lines are plain text inputs, and a few lines are JSON-stringified vectors (client pre-vectorized).

alex_engineer: Ah — mixed types in the same NDJSON batch. Our validator expects either text inputs or numeric arrays, not a mix where arrays are embedded as strings. If a line has a string containing brackets it remains a string token, so downstream shape check treats it as a text input and then the server tries to embed it -> results in dimension mismatch when we try to concat with precomputed vectors.

ingrid_research: Repro steps I ran locally: send three-line ndjson where line2 is stringified vector -> server returns 400 and logs show: \"expected vector length 1536 but got 1\". Repro curl: 
```
printf '%s\n' '{"input":"hello"}' '{"input":"[0.12,0.34,0.56]"}' '{"input":"world"}' | \\
  curl -sS -X POST https://local.redwood/v1/embeddings -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' --data-binary @-\n```

alex_engineer: Root cause: client mixing raw text and already-vectorized payloads in the same batch using the same field name. Our API allows sending precomputed vectors if you use the `vector` field (internal design), but the customer used `input` for everything. With NDJSON we treat each line independently but later we batch into a single tensor expecting consistent dtype/shape. Mixed types break batching.

maria_support: Customer also reported a billing spike because retries triggered. They switched to retries on 4xx and flooded us. They want a workaround asap.

jonathan_sre: Temporary mitigation for customer: 1) Stop client retries for 4xx until we confirm shape; 2) Send consistent payloads (all raw text or all vectors) or send two separate requests (one for precomputed vectors with `Content-Type: application/json` and top-level `vectors`) 3) As quick fix, they can switch to application/json with a top-level array so we don't mix stream lines. Example good JSON (vectors):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "input": [[0.12,0.34,0.56], [0.11,0.21,0.31]]
}
```
Or for text: 
```
{
  "input": ["hello","world"]
}
```

ingrid_research: Long-term: we should detect stringified arrays (a line where `input` is a string that looks like `^\[.*\]$`) and attempt a best-effort JSON.parse to turn it into numbers, but only as a permissive fallback with a warning header. Otherwise reject with a clearer 400: \"Mixed input types in batch — send all text or all vectors, or use `vector` field for precomputed embeddings.\"

alex_engineer: Added a unit test repro to the embed validator and a fix candidate: if Content-Type is application/x-ndjson, validate each line's type and return 400 with code `mixed_input_types` and a short message. I'll open PR with logs and sample error payload.

maria_support: I told ACME steps to stop retries and split their request into two consistent batches. They patched and confirmed the 400s stopped. They want us to patch server-side validation so it fails fast with a clear error and doesn't cause retries/billing.

api-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-384 - mixed-ndjson-embed-shape (assigned to alex_engineer).

ops-bot: Note — watch for billing anomalies from 2109876000-2109877000, rate limit + retries from ACME.

jonathan_sre: Follow-ups: (a) Alex to open PR for clearer error + detection. (b) Ingrid to draft fallback parse behavior under feature flag. (c) Support to send recommended examples/snippets to customer and confirm resolved.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll send the snips and confirm closure once ACME validates in prod :thumbsup:
